## Body

#350 (merged 4e5f77d8, coder/f281-fix). What I learned:
- bash 3.2 (macOS /bin/bash) drops a TERM that lands on a job it has just forked, while the child still carries the parent's TERM trap. Probe: 86/300 lost with one TERM, 0/300 when TERM is re-sent every 0.1 s. Any "TERM once, then wait" loop over a just-forked job is a latent hang: re-send each tick (a brake, own groups only).
- A race this narrow is rarely hit by the real-timing test (the old one-TERM mutant passed 5/5). Model it deterministically: a test binary that drops its first TERM (`trap 'trap - TERM' TERM`), and assert the stop beat the KILL escalation.
- Test fixtures that spawn scripts with `set -m` jobs must be detached (own group) and stopped at teardown by their group and their jobs' groups (ps ppid walk). Otherwise a failed or timed-out test leaves scripts with ppid 1 for hours.
- Reviewer B350-R1-01 (rule 6): a teardown Set of recorded groups must retire a group at its first observed absence, because its number can be reused. Only fresh ancestry from a running fixture re-adds it. Put signals behind an interface so the gone-then-reused case is a mocked unit test.
- harness checks' rust/smoke stages refuse under the 25 GB disk floor; that's environmental, so say so and cite CI.
- stop_bash on a vitest run SIGKILLs it, and afterEach never runs. Stop stress loops gently, or expect short orphans.
